data.summary: `ddflow wait --item B-hy-stop-protocol` exited 0 with 'READY ... `ddflow claim B-hy-stop-protocol` now' the moment B-res-merge-landed released, while `ddflow next --phase P-agent-hygiene` in the same minute still listed it '(blocked) conflict — globs overlap B-hy-phase-close offered in this plan'. The two readiness answers disagree: wait checks live leases only, next also applies the plan's offered-item overlap. An agent that trusts wait's instruction claims an item next calls blocked, which is the path B-claim-unavailable-fires-past-deps can force-approve silently. Expected: one readiness rule, or wait names the remaining plan-level conflict instead of saying claim now.
data.title: wait says READY and claim now while next still reports the item blocked

data.note: P-swarm push: pause and stop verbs, item.paused, rule in AGENTS.md, MCP instructions and deltas; held files added when free

data.body:
A ddflow pause <id> --note '<where I stopped, next step>' verb: commits WIP on the item's branch (never discards), records item.paused (state OPEN, worktree and branch kept, the note shown first in the next agent's brief) and releases the lease. ddflow stop (no id): for every item the agent holds, done work is merged and completed (gates allowing), the rest paused; prints what it did. The rule goes into AGENTS.md, the MCP instructions and every harness delta: before ending for any reason (tokens running out, compaction, end of turn, user stop) run ddflow stop. Nothing is pushed.

Coordinator 2026-11-05: `ddflow stop --auto` is in this item because B-hy-stop-hooks calls it. --auto is the unattended call from a harness hook, with nobody there: it pauses everything the agent holds and neither merges nor completes anything, so nothing lands without a person or agent looking at the gates. Plain `ddflow stop` is the one that finishes done work, and only on a verdict with no blocker. Globs widened to what the spec needs (operator route via coordinator); files live lanes hold (core/model.py, core/redact/log.py, README.md, goldens, event_kinds.json, test_coherence_coverage.py) are added with `update --globs` once free, never worked around.

data.claim: After a deliberate release, a claim by a DIFFERENT agent rebinds to the item's recorded tree and branch, with commits and uncommitted files intact, so pause needs no new tree handling.
data.falsifier: The second agent's claim is refused, or gets a new tree or branch, or the uncommitted file is gone.
data.mechanism: _h_lease_gone returns a RUNNING item to OPEN (fix-B601fa7eff9) and leaves item.worktree and item.branch set; claim_tree._recorded_tree rebinds to a recorded tree git still lists with that branch.

data.question: Does a released item keep its tree and branch so another agent's claim resumes it, leaving pause to add only the commit, the note and the event?

evidence.note: Claim: a released item's tree and branch survive and a different agent's claim rebinds to them. Probe in a throwaway repo with the real CLI: lane-b got the same tree and branch, rebound True, commit and uncommitted b.py intact. Research note recorded with the probe output.

Ran ddflow brief --item B-hy-stop-protocol; read r-surface-budget, r-replay-compat, r-agent-parity, r-docs-with-the-change, r-consent-outward, r-mode-parity, r-everything-configurable, r-bounded-everything, r-derive-dont-store, r-log-is-the-state. Lesson L-never-git-stash and the WIP-commit rule apply: pause commits, never stashes.
